description: fetched bytes against a registry content hash. The rule: hash the bytes as fetched, compare the result with the digest, check that the bytes are in canonical form, then check the CID. digestMatch, form and cid are the three answers; verified is true exactly when verdict is match. verdict is match only when the fetched bytes hash to the digest, are canonical, and the CID addresses them, is absent, or is not checkable without an IPFS node. unknown-form: the bytes hash to the digest but the canonicalization is unknown, so their form is unchecked. cid-mismatch: the bytes hash to the digest and are canonical, but the CID does not address them or is not a valid CID. form is canonical, not-canonical, unknown or invalid (not UTF-8 for JCS or LF text, or not I-JSON). not-canonical: the fetched bytes or their canonical form hash to the digest, but the fetched bytes are not canonical (pretty-printed JSON, a CR byte, a byte order mark); it is a failure. canonical-match: the same case with options.acceptCanonicalForm. member-match: only with options.pointer, or options.tryMembers, which tries each top-level member whose value is an object, in document order; it verifies that member only, never the rest of the file. mismatch: neither form hashes to the digest. invalid: the bytes cannot be read under the canonicalization. digestMatch: the fetched bytes as fetched hash to the digest. canonicalDigestMatch: the canonical bytes, of the whole file or of the member, do. cid is checked against the fetched bytes for scope whole and against the member's canonical bytes for scope member; canonicalCid against the canonical bytes when they differ from the fetched bytes, else null. Each is match, mismatch, not-checkable, absent or invalid.
